title: The layoff
premise: Two men with the same job and the same salary live one above the other. Every night one scrolls on the sofa and one learns AI skills at his desk. Then both are laid off on the same morning. One panics. One already has clients.

shots.image_prompt: front-on cutaway of a two-storey apartment building at night with its front wall taken off, the frame split into two rooms of exactly the same size stacked one above the other, a thick floor between them at the exact middle of the picture, dark blue night at the outer edges of the building. Both rooms have the same layout: a door on the left wall, a wooden desk with a desk lamp left of centre under an empty cork board, a window on the back wall showing a dark city skyline, a ceiling fan, a wall lamp on the right wall and a long grey three-seat sofa along the right wall, long enough to lie down on. Nothing is pinned on either cork board. Upstairs room, dim, the desk lamp switched off, the upstairs desk bare with no laptop on it and its chair empty and pushed in: {noah}, in a pale blue shirt and grey trousers, lying back on the long grey sofa on the right side of the room, far from the desk, his legs stretched out along the sofa, holding a phone up close to his face, the phone's cold blue light on his face. Downstairs room, warm and lit by the desk lamp: {eli}, in a mustard yellow shirt with the sleeves rolled up and dark trousers, sitting at the desk typing on an open laptop, a brown leather work bag on the floor by his chair, a small black and gold robot penguin desk toy with a glowing orange chest beside the laptop. Nobody else in the picture
shots.motion_prompt: The camera does not move at all. A busy, sped-up day in both rooms. Upstairs Noah gets up from the sofa, wanders to the window, comes back and flops down onto the sofa again, rolls onto his side, sits up, lies back, his thumb flicking the phone the whole time and the phone light flickering on his face; his cork board stays empty. Downstairs Eli types fast at his laptop, stands up and pins a bright coloured note on the cork board, sits and types again, takes a quick call, stands and pins another note, and another, until by the end the board is crowded with coloured notes. Both ceiling fans turn. Sounds: fast keyboard typing downstairs, the soft thump of the sofa and phone taps upstairs, a quiet room hum.

shots.image_prompt: wide front view of a bright open-plan office in warm morning sunlight, two desks side by side facing us, big windows and blurred co-workers far behind. At the left desk {noah}, in a pale blue shirt and grey trousers with an office lanyard round his neck, staring wide-eyed at the phone in his hand, his other hand gripping his hair. At the right desk {eli}, in a mustard yellow shirt with the sleeves rolled up and dark trousers with an office lanyard round his neck, reading his own phone with a calm, small smile. On each desk an empty cardboard box stands beside the keyboard, a monitor, a coffee mug and a small potted plant. Nobody else near the desks
shots.motion_prompt: Both phones buzz at the same moment and they look down at them, then react big. At the left desk Noah jolts upright, reads again, grabs his hair with both hands, spins his chair to look around the office and back, then slumps forward with his head down. At the right desk Eli reads, raises his eyebrows, nods slowly, then leans back in his chair with a small, calm smile. Their hands never pick anything up and nothing on the desks moves. Blurred people hurry past far behind. The camera pushes in very slowly on the two of them. Sounds: both phones buzz loudly at the same moment at the start, then Noah gasps and breathes hard, the office murmuring behind.

shots.motion_prompt: The camera does not move at all. Downstairs Eli talks to a client on his laptop, laughing and nodding, gesturing with both hands, then stands, pins one more note on the full board and gives a small fist pump, his room staying warm and bright to the very end. Upstairs Noah shifts restlessly on the sofa: scrolling, lying back, rolling over, scrolling. Halfway through, the light in the upstairs room slowly fades out until that whole room is black and the only thing still lit is his face, in the cold glow of the phone. Sounds: Eli's happy chatter and a laugh on the call downstairs, the faint tap of Noah's thumb on the glass upstairs, then quiet.
